messages:
lina: Heads up — noticed a perf regression on Mixtral MoE p95 after the new kernel-selector handoff change. posting traces + quick theory.
omar: ugh, which change? the auto-handoff to fused-kernel path?
sasha: yes that one. we saw lower median but higher tail. likely extra memcpy or serialization during expert switching.
zach: can you paste the profile? even a flame or hotlines helps.
lina: attaching condensed trace (trimmed). this is from one 8k token workload, 64 batch.
```
perf summary: p50 42ms p95 182ms p99 320ms
kernel-select: auto-handoff -> extra 4.2ms avg when expert-count>8
expert-kv-miss-rate: 3.4x baseline
memcpy/device-sync: spikes aligned w/ router-logit-updates
```
omar: interesting — expert kv miss sounds like cache pressure from parallelism. we changed expert-parallelism from 1 -> 2 on hot experts last week right?
sasha: correct. idea was to reduce router contention. but doubling parallelism increases working set across experts, evicting per-expert KV caches.
lina: hypothesis: kernel handoff adds small dispatch latency that interacts badly with higher KV eviction rate -> requests wait for KV load from host -> tail climbs.
zach: suggestion: try 2 experiments: 1) revert expert-parallelism for hot list to 1, keep kernel handoff. 2) keep parallelism=2 but switch kernel_policy to `sticky-fused` (avoid per-request handoff). compare p95.
omar: agree. also add a micro-batching tweak: lower `--batch-ms` from 10 -> 4 for topk routing paths to reduce wait-before-dispatch. could help tails if handoff is time-sensitive.
sasha: added quick config diffs:
```
# experiment A
moe.router.hot_expert_parallelism = 1
kernel.selector.policy = "auto-handoff" # unchanged

# experiment B
moe.router.hot_expert_parallelism = 2
kernel.selector.policy = "sticky-fused"
runtime.args = ["--batch-ms=4", "--kv-cache-evict-threshold=0.85"]
```
perf-bot: scheduled perf-run: exp-A @ 1975012400, exp-B @ 1975012420. will post traces when done. :robot_face:
lina: thanks. also instrument router logits to emit top-k softmax entropy over time — want to see if routing sharpness changed after the recent topk tweak. low entropy => concentrated routing => cache pressure.
zach: good call. add metric `moe.router.topk_entropy` and `moe.expert.kv_miss_ratio` to dashboards.
omar: FYI I profiled a single-hot case with kernel handoff off vs on: handoff adds ~3.9ms but only when expert-kv-miss > 0.2. So it's conditional.
sasha: that conditional behavior is the killer — if we can avoid handoff when kv_miss high we win. propose heur: if expert.kv_miss_ratio > 0.25 then force `sticky-fused` for that request. cheap check in router.
lina: love it. add small patch with gating flag and a fast path token to router decisions. nominating @zach to implement guard.
zach: on it. will prototype a guard and run microbench. timeline: 2 days.
perf-bot: exp-A results: p95=168ms (down from 182), kv_miss ratio down 1.6x. exp-B results: p95=150ms, but gpu util rose 6%. full traces in perf dashboard link: https://perf.redwood.internal/runs/1975012345
lina: great signal. looks like sticky-fused + parallelism wins but cost in util. we need cost vs latency tradeoff for Dedicated customers.
omar: next actions: (1) implement conditional-handoff gating, (2) run longer stochastics with production mix, (3) add RU/cost metric to rollout gating.
sasha: + add TTL-based KV shards for hot experts to lower churn (evict LRU beyond 2m).
zach: will open PR referencing this thread. thanks everyone. :thumbsup:
